answer: Hardware-rooted identity resists Sybil attacks: each agent must prove its identity is bound to one unique physical device, attested by a secure enclave whose ferrous casing and quartz clock give the chip an unclonable fingerprint. The enclave signs every transaction, and the network rejects any identity whose attestation signal cannot be verified against the manufacturer's public registry. Spawning a fake identity then requires buying real hardware, so a thousand Sybils cost a thousand chips.
